_comment: Travel guide for the Green Party Conference at the Brighton Centre, 2 to 4 October 2026. Shown in the Conference view until show_until. Walking minutes are computed from coordinates (straight line x 1.3 for streets, at 80 m a minute); tests/test_curated_data.py holds them to that.

venue.name: Brighton Centre
notes: On the seafront, with a rear entrance on Russell Road.
There is a security check at the door. Food and drink cannot be taken in, except for medical reasons.
No car park of its own. Blue Badge drop-off lay-bys are at the front and back.
Cycle racks at the front and rear.

nearest_stops.name: Clock Tower
nearest_stops.hint: top of West Street, 3 min walk

nearest_stops.name: Churchill Square
nearest_stops.hint: by the shopping centre, 3 min walk

arrivals.name: Brighton Station
arrivals.how: A 15 minute walk, downhill all the way: Queen's Road, then West Street to the sea. Or any bus from the station front to the Clock Tower (1, 6, 7, 12, 14, 27, 46, 48, 49 and others), about 5 minutes.
from_where: London Victoria and London Bridge: direct trains, about an hour.
Gatwick Airport: direct trains, about 30 minutes.
Southampton, Portsmouth, Chichester and Worthing (West Coastway): direct trains along the coast.
Eastbourne, Lewes and Hastings (East Coastway): direct trains, about 35 minutes from Eastbourne.

arrivals.name: Pool Valley coach station (Old Steine)
arrivals.how: National Express stops at Pool Valley, by the Old Steine gardens. The Brighton Centre is a 10 minute walk west along the seafront, or almost any bus heading west to the Clock Tower.

arrivals.name: Brighton Station, Stroudley Road
arrivals.how: FlixBus stops on Stroudley Road, behind Brighton Station, not at Pool Valley. Walk through to the station front (about 5 minutes), then down Queen's Road and West Street, or take a bus from the station front.

arrivals.name: Preston Park (London Road)
arrivals.how: Some FlixBus coaches also stop at Preston Park, about 2 km north. Bus 5 or 5A runs from there to Churchill Square.

text: The Brighton Centre has no car park, and Brighton has no park-and-ride.
The nearest car parks are Churchill Square (West Street, opposite the rear entrance, with the closest accessible bays) and Regency Square (under the square, 5 minutes west).
Parking in central Brighton is expensive and fills on busy days. If you can, park outside the city and come in by train or bus.

hotel_areas.name: Seafront, west of the venue (Regency Square, Kings Road)
Hove (Palmeira Square, Church Road, Western Road)
hotel_areas.note: Western Road is closed between Holland Road and Montpelier Road until 6 November. Brighton & Hove buses from Hove are diverted, and Norfolk Square and Brunswick Place are not served. Allow extra time.

hotel_areas.walk: 10 to 15 minutes, downhill to the venue.

on_site: Several socials are in the Brighton Centre itself (East Bar, Syndicate 1 and 2, Meeting Room 15). The Living Streets walk on Saturday meets at the Brighton Centre bus stop at 13:30.
tickets: Tap a contactless card or phone on the reader when you board. Brighton & Hove Buses cap what you pay in a day, so you never pay more than a day ticket.
A single fare in England is capped at £3.
Stagecoach (the 700 along the coast) has its own tickets; a Brighton & Hove day ticket is not valid on it.
accessibility: The Brighton Centre and the seafront are step-free. Read the venue's access statement for entrances and facilities.
Brighton Station to the venue is downhill one way and uphill the other. A bus from the station front to the Clock Tower avoids the climb back.
Every Brighton & Hove and Stagecoach bus here is low-floor with a wheelchair space.
Taxi ranks: Brighton Station front, and East Street near the Clock Tower.
late_night: Night buses run from the Clock Tower and North Street after the day services stop: N1, N5, N7, N12, N14 and N700 (along the coast to Worthing). Check the live board for the next one.
